newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close lower as mood turns cautious.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close lower as mood turns cautious.

text.p: French equities fell on Tuesday as investors took profits on the market's partial rebound from a sharp fall on Friday after U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan sounded a cautious note about stockmarket gains.

Traders said investors were also hesitant ahead of French President Jacques Chirac's scheduled television appearance on Thursday and potentially market-moving U.S. wholesale price data due out on Wednesday afternoon.
The bourse's blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 4.44 points or 0.2 percent at 2,251.40, while the CAC-40 futures contract fell three points to 2,257. Volume was 4.9 billion francs.
Traders said investors were feeling cautious after a recent rally that brought the index within striking distance last week of its all time record of 2,360.98.
A British broker in Paris said that although institutional investors had not sold off, Greenspan enjoyed widespread credibility and the markets would likely move more cautiously.
Chirac may reveal a cabinet reshuffle but is expected to retain the strong franc policy, offering little to seduce equities investors who would like a weaker French currency, one analyst said.
Lower U.S. and French bonds also fuelled profit-taking on Tuesday.
Shares in Alcatel Alsthom closed down 3.41 percent at 433.5 francs on the dim outlook for the group's CIT subsidiary.
Shares in oil group Total, another CAC heavyweight, eased 1.80 percent to 402.60 francs, pressured by refinery strikes.
Canal Plus shares fell 1.44 percent to 1,167 francs on the back of a negative article on its Spanish subsidiary.
Pechiney shares rose 3.4 percent to 210.40 francs, helped by news of European and U.S. asset sales.

Remy-Cointreau shares rose 0.73 percent to 138 francs. Although the drinks reported a drop in first-half pre-tax profit and a rise in its debt, its results were not as poor as some investors in the market had feared and its outlook was sanguine.
